note:
spec/rust_conformance_spec.rb's own fixture — the NAMED/declared bluebook query's own `order_by`/`limit` (kernel/query_ordering.rs, extracted from kernel/read_model.rs and now shared with kernel/named_query.rs, 2026-08-11), proven for real across the genuinely different shapes the real corpus declares, not a single trivial case: Account.HighBalance/StrictlyAbove/AtMost (a numeric `balance` field, an arg-bound where via `:floor`/`:cap`, asc AND desc), ATMCard.ByFee (a numeric `daily_fee` field with a REAL limit that actually truncates — 4 active cards in, 3 out), Customer.Suspended (a string `reference` field, `desc`, plus a `limit 50` that does NOT truncate — proving a non-binding limit still runs the same code path without dropping a row it shouldn't), and Account.Open/Reachable (order_by :number — see below on why those two are included for real declared-query coverage rather than because they prove reordering). Every account/card number below is chosen so IDENTITY order (ascending by id, the TIER-1 base every answer sorts by first) and the DECLARED order genuinely diverge — acct-1/2/3/4/5 hold balances 700/300/1000/0/500 respectively, in that identity order, so a query that actually sorted them would visibly reshuffle that sequence, not just happen to already agree with it (the corner a lazy fixture — one whose identity order and value order coincide by accident — would silently fail to catch). Account.Open/Reachable are the one exception: both order by `:number`, which IS this aggregate's own `identified_by` field, so their declared order is PROVABLY identical to the identity tier by construction, not by coincidence — included anyway because they are two more real corpus queries this generator now covers, and the where-clause/status-filtering they exercise (Open's plain equality, Reachable's `in` comparator) is still real, even though their own order_by adds nothing beyond what identity already gave.

Account shapes: acct-1 (bal 700, open), acct-2 (bal 300, open), acct-3 (bal 1000, open), acct-4 (bal 0, closed — Money defaults to 0 cents, so CloseAccount's own "an account closes empty" given is satisfied with no Credit at all), acct-5 (bal 500, frozen). HighBalance(floor 400) matches {1,3,5} (2 and 4 fall below/at the floor) ordered desc by balance: 3(1000), 1(700), 5(500) — visibly NOT the identity-filtered order (1, 3, 5). StrictlyAbove(floor 500, gt not gte) matches {1,3} only (5's own 500 is excluded — the gt/gte boundary case), desc: 3(1000), 1(700). AtMost(cap 600) matches {2,4,5} (0/300/500 all sit at-or-under the cap, frozen/closed included — AtMost declares no status filter at all, matching Ruby's own `where(balance: {lte: :cap})` exactly), asc: 4(0), 2(300), 5(500) — again NOT the identity-filtered order (2, 4, 5). Reachable (status in "open,frozen") matches {1,2,3,5}, excluding only closed acct-4. Open (status eq "open") matches {1,2,3} only, excluding both frozen acct-5 and closed acct-4.

ATMCard shapes: four cards on acct-1, issued in serial order card-w/x/y/z with fees 5.0/1.0/4.0/2.0 respectively, all Activated (ByFee's own `where(status: "active")` — an issued-but-never-activated card would be silently excluded, which this fixture does not exercise since every card here IS activated). ByFee (order_by :daily_fee asc, limit 3) expected: card-x(1.0), card-z(2.0), card-y(4.0) — card-w(5.0) genuinely dropped by the limit, not merely reordered past the end coincidentally (4 candidates in, exactly 3 out, the highest-fee one missing).

Customer shapes: cust-1/cust-2 stay active; cust-3/cust-4 are Suspended. Suspended (order_by :reference desc, limit 50) matches {cust-3, cust-4}, desc-ordered as cust-4, cust-3 — the reverse of their own identity-ascending order, proving TIER 2's `desc` reversal fires on a STRING field (every numeric case above already proves it on a number); `limit 50` against only 2 real rows proves a limit that never binds still runs `query_ordering::apply`'s own truncate step without dropping anything it shouldn't.
